newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore October exports show glimmer of light.
newsitem.headline: Singapore October exports show glimmer of light.

text.p: Singapore's non-oil exports rose a nominal 1.1 percent year-on-year in October, giving a glimmer of hope that the export slump could have ended.
The Trade Development Board released the data on Wednesday, saying in a statement that non-oil exports totalled Singapore $7.68 billion (US$5.45 billion) in October.
The figure was an improvement over a 6.2 percent fall in September and a 6.3 percent decline in August.
A Reuters poll had an average forecast of a year-on-year decline of 1.4 percent in October.
Although economists generally expected a better showing than in August and September, their estimates had varied widely from a fall of 5.3 percent year-on-year to a rise of three percent.

"This month's export figures should herald some recovery in the economy but the extent of the rebound is extremely hard to predict," Tan Min Lan, economist at Merrill Lynch in Singapore, said during the poll.

Based on a three-month moving average percentage change, non-oil domestic exports to the United States decreased by 3.3 percent to reach S$2.2 billion in October, the TDB said. The decrease was reflected in computer parts and peripherals, printers, digital CPUs for microcomputers, parts of colour televisions, radios and video cassette recorders.

Non-oil domestic exports to Malaysia were weak in October, falling by 7.0 percent to S$965 million based on a three-month moving average percentage change. On the same basis, non-oil domestic exports to Japan fell 13.8 percent to S$720 million.
Singapore's exports had slumped over the last six months due to a slowdown in the electronics industry in the United States and Japan.
Electronics, computers and related products account for about half of the island's total industrial production and almost 60 percent of its non-oil exports.
The dependence on the electronics industry had dragged Singapore's gross domestic product growth down to 3.2 percent in the third quarter, from 11.4 percent in the first three months of the year.
